newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - April 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday business - April 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- REGAN PUSHES CWS DESTRUCT BUTTON

Entrepreneur Andrew Regan is backing calls for a special general meeting which would vote to convert the Co-operative Wholesale Society into a company and then sell him its best businesses. He will ask 10 corporate members of the CWS, who support his proposals, to call the meeting. Regan will begin his campaign later this week.
-- REID OFFERS HIMSELF AS SEARS SACRIFICE

Chairman of Sears, Robert Reid, is considering offering himself for re-election at the annual meeting in June to end what he claims is "a whispering campaign" targeted at the group. He was responding to City reports that Sears' chief executive Liam Strong and he were about to be axed by the non-executive directors.
-- NEW LOOK GROOMED FOR A NEW FLOAT

Three years after women's fashion retailer New Look was shunned by the City during an attempt to float, the company is to try again. This time the chain will come to the market with new management and has been valued at 250 million stg, more than 100 million stg higher than the previous price tag.
-- CORDIANT SEEKING TO DEMERGE BATES

The board of advertising agency Cordiant is considering plans to demerge one of its two international advertising networks, Bates Worldwide, which accounts for 40 per cent of the group's business. Options under review include a straight demerger, partial demerger or merging Bates with an agency of similar size and floating off the new business.
-- ENERGY GROUP MAKES $1.2 BILLION BID

Coal and electricity company The Energy Group Plc has tabled a bid worth up to $1.2 billion dollars for New England Electric Systems, a major power station group in the US. If successful, the bid would be the largest inroad yet made by a British electricity group into the vast US market.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- STRONG TO QUIT AFTER SEARS IS BROKEN UP

Chief executive of Sears, Liam Strong, is working on a break-up plan which would separate the group's successful businesses, such as Selfridges, from the British Shoe Corporation, the troubled shoe business. Once the break-up is complete Strong will step down. He has come under increasing criticism from investors and analysts.
-- LONDON SHARES FACE TEST OF NERVE AFTER DOW DIPS

Wall Street's plunge on Friday, triggered by inflation worries after a jump in producer prices, will signal a shaky start for London shares tomorrow, and could mark the beginning of a period of market nerves lasting beyond the general election.
-- GEC IN TALKS WITH US DEFENCE GIANT

The General Electric Company is believed to be in talks with Lockheed Martin, the world's largest military and aerospace combine, about a transatlantic alliance that would intensify the reshaping of the U.S. and European defence industries. Experts believe a deal would not involve cross-shareholding or full joint-venture status.
-- BUSINESS RATES MOVE GIVES MAJOR AN EDGE OVER BLAIR

Results from the NatWest /Manchester Business School show that small firms could face a larger tax burden under Labour than under the Conservatives. The results show that although there is little difference in the impact on small firms from the two main parties' business proposals, a marginally lower tax burden will fall on sole traders and partnerships under Tory taxation pledges.
THE OBSERVER -- BT FACES 277 MILLION STG BILL IF MERGER IS DITCHED

A 13 billion stg deal struck by British Telecom directors to create Concert, the fourth largest telecoms company, threatens to land shareholders with a 277 million stg bill if they reject the planned merger with US telecoms company MCI. BT promised to pay MCI 277 million stg plus expenses if the tie-up fails to win backing.
-- TORIES REVEL IN PSBR FIGURES

Chancellor Kenneth Clarke is expected to seize on better- than-forecast borrowing figures, due on Wednesday, to proclaim a dramatic improvement in the public finances. He is to use the data to counter Labour claims that the Tories have been bad housekeepers and to calm fears of steep post-election tax rises.
-- HOMEBUYERS FACE DOUBLE WAMMY

Irrespective of who wins the general election homeowners could be hit by rising mortgage rates and the withdrawal of mortgage tax relief. The Tories have not made a committment to retain Miras in their election manifesto and the Labour Party's makes no mention of it.
-- CASINOS GET CHANCE TO PUT ON THE RITZ

Owners of the Ritz, the Barclay twins, are seeking a new casino to occupy the basement of the luxury hotel. Several potential tenants, including Rank, the casino operator, have been shown the premises. The brothers will offer the use of the Ritz name as part of the deal.
-- BRANSON TO BUY BACK RADIO SHARES

Virgin Group, owned by Richard Branson, is buying back the remaining shares in its Virgin Radio venture in a deal worth 80 million stg. The buy-back option will allow start-up shareholders including banker JP Morgan, venture capital company Apax and Sir David Frost to cash in on their initial investment.
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY
-- SFO ON TRAIL OF 100 MILLION STG INSURANCE FRAUDSTERS

The Serious Fraud Office has begun an investigation into a 100 million stg fraud. The SFO will join Belgian police and the FBI in the hunt for the conspirators behind a network of fraudulent companies that stole tens of millions of pounds stg from brokers and insurers in London and the US between 1989 and 1996.
-- THAMES PLANS 800 MILLION STG RESERVOIR

Thames Water, as part of its long-term strategic programme for maintaining water supplies to its customers, is drawing up plans for a new 800 million stg reservoir. Without the reservoir, the company is concerned that London and the Thames region could face water shortages by early in the next century.
-- BROKERS ACT TO HEAD OFF WINDFALL CHAOS

Barclays Stockbrokers Limited claims that windfall share issues from demutualised building societies and insurance firms during the summer and autumn threaten chaos for the stock market, due to the quantity of paper generated. BSL has prepared for a flood of share transactions by setting up an "alternative call centre" with BT.
-- SAUDI EYES ON MAYFAIR

It is believed that Prince al-Waleed bin Talal is considering buying prime location property in London's Mayfair and Knightsbridge. The Prince has tabled a bid of 100 million stg for several properties in the BP Pension Fund portfolio that were put up for sale last month.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- 2000 BUG TAKES ITS TOLL NOW

Insurer Scottish Widows is refusing to buy shares in companies that are not preparing for possible computer problems in the year 2000. The company says it has already sold shares in several firms that are not ready to deal with the problem. The insurer is concerned that systems failures could wipe millions off the value of businesses in which they invest.
-- UNITED IN PAYING THE BILLS

The Constitutional Unit claims that if the Labour Party wins the election taxpayers will be expected to pay for Scottish and Welsh assemblies, which could cost 95 million stg a year. Labour claims there will be no extra tax bills because the assemblies will receive money saved by reducing quangos.
-- BANKS FEELING QUEASY

The Serious Fraud Office is investigating more than 20 companies who sold whisky and champagne as investments. High Street banks fear they will have to pay compensation to customers who lost money in such deals. Barclays and NatWest authorised several to accept credit cards.
-- WH SMITH MAY PLAY CARDS

Bill Cockburn, chief executive of WH Smith, is considering proposals to follow Marks & Spencer, Tesco and Sainsbury and sell financial services. He is attracted to customer loyalty through a range of financial offers led by an own-brand credit card, which carries points that could be exchanged for goods. The plans may involve Smith returning to the travel agency business.
